question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
By hook or by crook
(SICPO Paper I 2022)
options: Using whatever methods are necessary
Probably possible, but it will be difficult
Making more of an effort
Using a lot of energy and effort to do something
solution:
The correct answer is: Using whatever methods are necessary

Explanation:
"By hook or by crook" - "किसी भी तरह से / जैसे-तैसे करके"
This idiom means achieving something by any means possible, whether fair or unfair. The correct option fits because it conveys the idea of using all necessary methods to accomplish a goal, regardless of difficulty or morality.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase likely originates from medieval England, where "hook" and "crook" referred to tools used by peasants to gather firewood. "Hook" was a curved blade, and "crook" was a shepherd's staff. Over time, it evolved to mean achieving something by any means, lawful or otherwise.

Example:
"She was determined to win the competition by hook or by crook."
"वह प्रतियोगिता जीतने के लिए किसी भी तरह से तैयार थी।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "By hook or by crook" is "Using whatever methods are necessary" because it emphasizes achieving a goal through any possible means. The other options do not fully capture the idiom's essence of determination and willingness to use all strategies.

question:
What does the idiom 'Throw in the towel' mean?.
(Junior Engineer Civil)
options: To motivate someone to achieve a lot
To initiate a new challenge
To give up after realising success is impossible
To raise one's voice against the discussion
solution:
The correct answer is: To give up after realising success is impossible

Explanation:
"Throw in the towel" - "हार मान लेना"
This idiom means to admit defeat or surrender when one realizes that further effort is futile. It fits the context of giving up after recognizing that success is no longer possible.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase originates from boxing, where a trainer or cornerman would literally throw a towel into the ring to signal that their fighter could no longer continue, thereby conceding the match.

Example:
"After failing the exam three times, he decided to throw in the towel and pursue a different career."
"तीन बार परीक्षा में असफल होने के बाद, उसने हार मान ली और एक अलग करियर अपनाने का फैसला किया।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "Throw in the towel" is "To give up after realising success is impossible" because it signifies surrendering when further effort seems pointless. The other options do not align with the idiom's meaning.

question:
Select the correct meaning of the idiom "Run around in circles" from the given options:
(Group D posts)
options: putting efforts into something that is not a worthwhile result
to be extremely organized to get a desired result
circling into something and getting to a safe place
putting efforts into something and getting a desirable result
solution:
The correct answer is: putting efforts into something that is not a worthwhile result

Explanation:
"Run around in circles" - "बिना किसी सार्थक परिणाम के प्रयास करना"
This idiom means expending a lot of effort without making any real progress or achieving a meaningful outcome.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase likely originates from the literal act of running in circles, which involves continuous movement without reaching a destination. Over time, it evolved into a metaphor for futile or unproductive efforts.

Example:
"Instead of solving the problem, the team kept running around in circles, wasting time on unnecessary discussions."
"समस्या का समाधान करने के बजाय, टीम बेकार की चर्चाओं में समय बर्बाद करते हुए बिना किसी नतीजे के प्रयास करती रही।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "run around in circles" is "putting efforts into something that is not a worthwhile result" because it signifies futile actions without meaningful progress. The other options do not align with the idiom's intended meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom/phrase.
I had heard of henpecked husbands and now, I felt that I saw one.
(Combined Graduate Level Examination Tier I )
options: Oppressed husband
Dominating husbands
Controlling husband
Bossy husbands
solution:
The correct answer is: Oppressed husband

Explanation:
"Henpecked husband" - "मुर्गाबाज पति"
The idiom "henpecked husband" refers to a man who is constantly nagged, controlled, or dominated by his wife, making him feel oppressed or submissive.

Origin of the Idiom:
The term comes from the behavior of hens, which peck at weaker or subordinate birds to assert dominance. Similarly, a "henpecked husband" is metaphorically pecked at (nagged or controlled) by his wife.

Example:
"Ramesh is such a henpecked husband that he can't even go out without his wife's permission."
"रमेश इतना मुर्गाबाज पति है कि वह बिना पत्नी की इजाज़त के बाहर भी नहीं जा सकता।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "henpecked husband" is "oppressed husband" because it describes a man who is constantly dominated by his wife. The other options describe dominating or controlling individuals, which is the opposite of the idiom's meaning.

question:
Identify the sentence that provides the meaning of the given idiom.

Under the cloud
(Combined Graduate Level Examination Tier I 2023)
options: It was the best place to sit under the sky with hands full of food.
The driver was under suspicion after the police found blood on his car.
The Red fort looks beautiful amidst the cloudy weather and cold atmosphere.
The classmates were dancing together under the rain.
solution:
The correct answer is: The driver was under suspicion after the police found blood on his car.

Explanation:
"Under the cloud" - "संदेह में होना"
The idiom "under the cloud" means to be under suspicion or facing distrust. In this context, the driver is suspected because of the blood found on his car, making this sentence the best fit for the idiom's meaning.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase likely originates from the metaphorical use of a "cloud" representing suspicion or trouble hanging over someone. Just as a dark cloud can obscure clarity, suspicion can obscure a person's reputation.

Example:
"The politician remained under the cloud of corruption allegations for years."
"वह राजनेता वर्षों तक भ्रष्टाचार के आरोपों के संदेह में रहा।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "The driver was under suspicion after the police found blood on his car." is "being doubted or under suspicion" because the idiom refers to a state of distrust. The other options describe literal situations involving clouds or weather, unrelated to the idiom's figurative meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Rags to riches
(JSA(JNV Cadre))
options: Dress in expensive clothes
Make new dresses from old clothes
Rise from poverty to great wealth
Lose wealth and becoming poor
solution:
The correct answer is: Rise from poverty to great wealth

Explanation:
"Rags to riches" - "गरीबी से अमीरी तक का सफर"
The idiom "rags to riches" describes a person's journey from extreme poverty (rags) to great wealth (riches). The correct option fits this meaning perfectly, as it highlights a dramatic improvement in financial status.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase likely originated in the 19th century, inspired by real-life success stories of individuals who overcame poverty to achieve prosperity. It became popular in literature and media, symbolizing the classic underdog narrative.

Example:
"His rags-to-riches story inspired many young entrepreneurs."
"उनकी गरीबी से अमीरी तक की कहानी ने कई युवा उद्यमियों को प्रेरित किया।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "rags to riches" is "rise from poverty to great wealth" because it captures the essence of a dramatic financial transformation. The other options either misinterpret the idiom or are unrelated to its true meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.To look black
(MTS Non Tech Havaldar CBIC and CBN Examination 2024 )
options: To give an approving expression
To cry bitterly
To roll on ice
To seem unfavourable
solution:
The correct answer is: To seem unfavourable

Explanation:
"To look black" - "प्रतिकूल दिखाई देना"
This idiom means to appear negative, threatening, or unfavourable. It is often used to describe a situation or expression that suggests disapproval or bad prospects.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase likely originates from the association of the color black with darkness, gloom, and negativity in English idioms. Historically, black has been used metaphorically to represent misfortune or hostility.

Example:
"The economic forecast looks black for small businesses this year."
"इस साल छोटे व्यवसायों के लिए आर्थिक पूर्वानुमान प्रतिकूल दिख रहा है।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "To look black" is "To seem unfavourable" because it conveys a sense of negativity or disapproval. The other options do not align with the idiom's intended meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Bone to pick
(Constable GD Examination 2022)
options: Cleaning the floor for any garbage
Having a complaint that needs to be discussed
Making a feast
Having a fond memory to tell
solution:
The correct answer is: Having a complaint that needs to be discussed

Explanation:
"Bone to pick" - "शिकायत होना या विवाद का मुद्दा होना"
This idiom means having an issue or grievance that needs to be addressed. It implies that there is something unresolved that needs discussion, much like a dog gnawing on a bone until it's fully dealt with.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase likely originates from the image of a dog stubbornly chewing on a bone, unwilling to let go. Over time, it evolved to represent a persistent issue or argument that someone wants to settle.

Example:
"I have a bone to pick with you about the unfinished project."
"मेरी तुमसे अधूरे प्रोजेक्ट को लेकर एक शिकायत है।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "Bone to pick" is "Having a complaint that needs to be discussed" because it refers to an unresolved issue requiring attention. The other options do not relate to the idiom's intended meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom
To beat around the bush
(Workshop Attendant)
options: To avoid talking about the main issue or problem
To explore or wander in a forest or wilderness
To hit or strike something with a stick or branch
To compete or race with someone in a circular track
solution:
The correct answer is: To avoid talking about the main issue or problem

Explanation:
"To beat around the bush" - "मुद्दे से भटकना"
This idiom means to avoid addressing the main topic directly, often by discussing irrelevant or less important details instead.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase originates from hunting practices, where hunters would literally beat bushes to scare birds or animals out into the open. However, those who "beat around the bush" instead of going straight for the target were seen as hesitant or indirect.

Example:
"Stop beating around the bush and tell me what you really think!"
"इतना मुद्दे से भटकना बंद करो और सीधे बताओ कि तुम सच में क्या सोचते हो!"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "To beat around the bush" is "To avoid talking about the main issue or problem" because it signifies evading the main point. The other options describe literal actions unrelated to the idiom's figurative meaning.

question:
Choose the correct meaning of the underlined idiomatic expression in the following sentence:
The manager decided to cut to the chase and address the main issues during the meeting.
(Craft Instructor Sewing Technology (For Degree Diploma Holders))
options: avoid the main issue
delete some information
get straight to the point
find a practical solution
solution:
The correct answer is: get straight to the point

Explanation:
"Cut to the chase" - "मुख्य मुद्दे पर सीधे आना"
The idiom "cut to the chase" means to skip unnecessary details and focus directly on the most important part of a discussion. In the given sentence, the manager wants to address the main issues without wasting time, which aligns perfectly with this meaning.

Origin of the Idiom:
This phrase originates from early Hollywood films, where action-packed chase scenes were often the most exciting parts. Directors would "cut to the chase" to skip slower dialogue and get to the thrilling part, eventually evolving into a metaphor for getting to the main point quickly.

Example:
"Instead of small talk, let’s cut to the chase and discuss the budget."
"बेकार की बातें करने के बजाय, सीधे मुख्य मुद्दे पर आते हैं और बजट पर चर्चा करते हैं।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "cut to the chase" is "get straight to the point" because it emphasizes skipping irrelevant details and focusing on the core issue. The other options either contradict the idiom's meaning or are unrelated.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Break the ice
(Maharashtra Municipal Taxation and Administration Service)
options: To create an awkward situation
To break something into pieces
To initiate a conversation
To enjoy drinking wine
solution:
The correct answer is: To initiate a conversation

Explanation:
"Break the ice" - "बर्फ़ तोड़ना (बातचीत शुरू करना)"
This idiom means to relieve initial tension or awkwardness in a social situation by starting a conversation or doing something to make people feel more comfortable.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase likely originates from the practice of breaking ice to clear a path for ships in frozen waters, symbolizing the removal of barriers to communication. Over time, it evolved into a metaphor for easing social interactions.

Example:
"At the party, John told a joke to break the ice and make everyone feel at ease."
"पार्टी में, जॉन ने बर्फ़ तोड़ने (बातचीत शुरू करने) के लिए एक चुटकुला सुनाया ताकि सभी सहज महसूस करें।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "Break the ice" is "To initiate a conversation" because it refers to starting an interaction to reduce tension. The other options do not relate to the idiom's intended meaning.

question:

(CHSL 2021 Tier I)
options: To express loyalty, respect, or support for something insincerely
To face a risk
To pretend to be very old
To ignore what someone is saying
solution:
The correct answer is: To express loyalty, respect, or support for something insincerely

Explanation:
"To pay lip service" - "मुंह से हाँ में हाँ मिलाना (केवल दिखावे के लिए)"
This idiom means to say that you support or agree with something without actually doing anything to prove it. The correct option fits because it captures the insincere nature of the expression.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase likely originated from the idea of "lip" (mouth) being used to speak words of support or loyalty ("service") without any real action or commitment behind them. It emphasizes the hollowness of verbal assurances.

Example:
"Many politicians pay lip service to environmental issues but do nothing to address them."
"कई नेता पर्यावरण के मुद्दों पर केवल मुंह से हाँ में हाँ मिलाते हैं, लेकिन उन्हें हल करने के लिए कुछ नहीं करते।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "To pay lip service" is "To express loyalty, respect, or support for something insincerely" because it refers to empty words without genuine intent. The other options describe unrelated concepts.

options: To thrive or to grow very successfully

solution:

"The soldiers held the enemy at bay until reinforcements arrived."

The correct meaning of "Hold someone or something at bay" is "Prevent someone or something from moving closer" because it accurately describes the act of keeping a threat or unwanted presence away. The other options do not align with the idiom's intended meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Hands down
(Constable GD 2021)
options: Very weakly and slowly
Without any weapons
With sufficient strength
Easily and without doubt
solution:
The correct answer is: Easily and without doubt

Explanation:
"Hands down" - "बिना किसी संदेह के आसानी से"
The idiom "hands down" means achieving something effortlessly or without any doubt. It implies a clear and undisputed victory or success.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase originates from horse racing, where a jockey who is winning comfortably may relax and lower ("hands down") the reins, indicating an easy victory without needing to push the horse further. Over time, it evolved to mean any effortless or undisputed success.

Example:
"She won the debate hands down—her arguments were unbeatable."
"उसने बहस बिना किसी संदेह के जीत ली—उसके तर्क अजेय थे।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "hands down" is "easily and without doubt" because it conveys an undisputed or effortless accomplishment. The other options do not align with the idiom's intended meaning.

options: Safe and dangerous place

solution:

Explanation:
"Weal and woe" - "सुख और दुःख"
The idiom "weal and woe" refers to both good times (prosperity, happiness) and bad times (misfortune, sorrow). It signifies the ups and downs of life.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase comes from Old English, where "weal" meant well-being or prosperity, and "woe" meant sorrow or distress. Together, they represent the dual nature of life's experiences.

Example:
"A true friend stands by you through weal and woe."
"एक सच्चा दोस्त सुख-दुःख में आपका साथ देता है।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "weal and woe" is "prosperity and misfortune" because it captures the essence of life's contrasting experiences. The other options do not convey the intended duality of happiness and sorrow.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.
Despite their differences, the two politicians decided to ________ and work together for the greater good.
(CGLE 2023 Tier II Paper I Extra Time)
options: burn the midnight oil
bury the hatchet
bark up the wrong tree
blow off steam
solution:
The correct answer is: bury the hatchet

Explanation:
The idiom "bury the hatchet" means to make peace or end a conflict, which fits perfectly in the context of politicians putting aside their differences to work together.

Let's Explain All IDIOMS & Their Meanings:

burn the midnight oil – देर रात तक काम करना – To work late into the night.
Example: "She had to burn the midnight oil to finish her project before the deadline."

bury the hatchet – झगड़ा खत्म करना / शांति स्थापित करना – To stop arguing and make peace.
Example: "After years of rivalry, the two families finally buried the hatchet."

bark up the wrong tree – गलत दिशा में प्रयास करना – To pursue a mistaken or misguided course of action.
Example: "If you think I stole your book, you're barking up the wrong tree."

blow off steam – गुस्सा या तनाव कम करना – To release pent-up energy or frustration.
Example: "After a stressful day at work, he went to the gym to blow off steam."

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "bury the hatchet" is "to end a conflict and make peace" because the sentence describes politicians resolving their differences to collaborate. The other idioms do not fit the context of reconciliation.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Draw first blood

(Constable GD 2021)
options: Be the first to gain an advantage or score against an opponent
Take a blood test early in the morning
Agree to accompany someone for the diagnosis of an illness
Be the first to donate blood to help a friend
solution:
The correct answer is: Be the first to gain an advantage or score against an opponent

Explanation:
"Draw first blood" - "प्रतिद्वंद्वी पर पहला लाभ या अंक हासिल करना"
This idiom means to be the first to gain an advantage over an opponent, whether in sports, competition, or conflict. It metaphorically refers to causing the first injury or setback to the other side.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase originates from combat sports like boxing or fencing, where "drawing blood" (making an opponent bleed) signifies the first successful strike. Over time, it evolved to represent any initial advantage in a competitive scenario.

Example:
"In the debate, the opposition drew first blood by exposing the flaw in the government's policy."
"बहस में, विपक्ष ने सरकार की नीति में खामी उजागर करके पहला लाभ हासिल किया।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "Draw first blood" is "Be the first to gain an advantage or score against an opponent" because it signifies initiating a successful move in a competitive situation. The other options are unrelated to the idiom's metaphorical meaning.

The phrase originates from the idea that freshly made pancakes (hot cakes) are highly desirable and sell rapidly at markets or fairs. Over time, it became a metaphor for anything that is in high demand and sells out fast.

The correct meaning of "sold like hot cakes" is "sold quickly and in large numbers" because it perfectly describes the rapid and high-volume sales of the plots. The other options do not align with the idiom's intended meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
A man of means
(Constable GD Examination 2022)
options: A wealthy man with lots of money and assets
A well-mannered man with noble behaviour
Someone who is an iconic personality for youngsters
Someone who has earned a lot of fame
solution:
The correct answer is: A wealthy man with lots of money and assets

Explanation:
"A man of means" - "धनवान व्यक्ति"
The idiom refers to a person who has substantial financial resources or wealth. The word "means" here signifies financial capability or resources, making the first option the most accurate.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase "man of means" dates back to the 18th century, where "means" was commonly used to denote wealth or financial resources. It emphasizes a person's economic status rather than their character or fame.

Example:
"After years of hard work, he became a man of means and could afford a luxurious lifestyle."
"कड़ी मेहनत के बाद, वह एक धनवान व्यक्ति बन गया और एक आलीशान जीवन जीने में सक्षम हो गया।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "A man of means" is "A wealthy man with lots of money and assets" because the idiom specifically refers to financial prosperity. The other options describe personality traits or fame, which are unrelated to the idiom's true meaning.

question:
Select the appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Last resort
(CHSL Exam 2024 Tier I)
options: Last friend remaining
Last hotel on the way
Last ride
Last course of action
solution:
The correct answer is: Last course of action

Explanation:
"Last resort" - "आखिरी उपाय"
The idiom "last resort" refers to the final option or action taken when all other possibilities have failed. It signifies the ultimate solution in a difficult situation.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase originates from the legal and military term "resort," meaning a place or method of seeking help. Over time, it evolved to represent the final option when no other alternatives remain.

Example:
"If negotiations fail, going to court will be our last resort."
"यदि वार्ता विफल हो जाती है, तो अदालत जाना हमारा आखिरी उपाय होगा।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "last resort" is "last course of action" because it signifies the final option when all others have been exhausted. The other options are unrelated to the idiom's intended meaning.
